message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the **federal public holidays** in Canada for 2023. (Note that each province/territory may add its own holidays on top of these.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Day of Week |
|---------|-------------|-------------|
| New Year’s Day | January 1 (Sunday) | Sunday – observed Monday, Jan 2 |
| Family Day (BC, AB, SK, NB, ON) | February 20 (Monday) | Monday |
| Good Friday | April 7 (Friday) | Friday |
| Easter Monday (Federal employees only) | April 10 (Monday) | Monday |
| Victoria Day | May 22 (Monday) | Monday |
| Canada Day | July 1 (Saturday) | Saturday – observed Monday, Jul 3 |
| Civic Holiday (varies by province) | First Monday in August (Aug 7) | Monday |
| Labour Day | September 4 (Monday) | Monday |
| Thanksgiving Day | October 9 (Monday) | Monday |
| Remembrance Day | November 11 (Wednesday) | Wednesday – observed Thursday, Nov 12 |
| Christmas Day | December 25 (Monday) | Monday |
| Boxing Day | December 26 (Tuesday) | Tuesday |

### How to use this in your app
1. **Store the dates** in a database or a JSON file so you can reference them programmatically.  
2. **Handle observed days**: For holidays that fall on a weekend, Canada observes the following weekday (e.g., New Year’s Day 2023 falls on Sunday, so the observed day is Monday, Jan 2).  
3. **Add provincial holidays**: If you need province‑specific holidays (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Ontario, National Indigenous Peoples Day in BC), you’ll need to pull those from a separate source or maintain a mapping per province.

Let me know if you’d like a more detailed list that includes provincial holidays or if you need help integrating this data into your codebase!
